best_for: Note takers who left Notion over privacy and want their pages encrypted on their own devices, and who can be trusted to store a 12-word key safely.

points.title: Your key is the account
points.text: There is no email or password. The app makes a 12-word recovery phrase on your device, and that phrase is how you log in everywhere. Anytype keeps no copy, so if you lose it on every device, nobody can open your vault, the company included.

points.title: Free first, paid for room
points.text: There is a Free tier and several paid memberships. Paid plans add sync storage, unlimited shared channels and a custom ANY ID used in web publishing links. Students and faculty get 50% off. The docs leave exact prices to the pricing page on anytype.io, so check it before you pick a plan.

points.title: Local-first, with a local-only option
points.text: By default your data syncs between devices through an encrypted backup node. An experimental local-only mode turns the node off, so devices sync only on the same local network. In that mode a lost or broken device means lost data, so backups are up to you.

points.title: Usage analytics cannot be switched off
points.text: The docs say the app sends anonymous usage events and crash reports, and there is no opt-out yet. They also say the content you write is never readable to them. Blocking the analytics hosts or building the app yourself are the only ways around it today.

points.title: Source available, not open source
points.text: The desktop code is public under the Any Source Available License 1.0. Personal, research and other non-commercial use is fine. Commercial use is allowed only on networks the Any Association approves, so it is not an OSI open-source license.

points.title: Getting data out
points.text: Export works to Markdown, PDF, HTML and the app's own Any-Block format, in JSON or Protobuf. If a paid membership ends, people in your shared spaces are asked to delete or export them, and exported spaces no longer sync.

points.title: Versions kept on this site
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 68 versions of the 64-bit installer. macOS (Intel and Apple Silicon, macOS 12 or later) and Linux list only the current release, so downgrades there need another source. The Flathub build is marked verified as published by Any Association.
